task.description:
WF-02 Step Final -- Git merge for REQ-367 (CD to QA on merge). Claim this handoff (status IN_PROGRESS). Follow docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md exactly: rebase feature/WF02-REQ367-20260917 onto latest origin/main, open a PR, wait for CI (both backend and frontend gates) to go green -- poll actively and synchronously (e.g. gh pr checks <PR#> in a bounded loop), do not rely on an internally-armed background monitor. If CI fails on something unrelated to this run's own diff (the known pre-existing A9 requirement_status_invariants_test.exs drift or similar), follow GIT_MERGE.md's documented handling. Once green, merge via gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch (or the documented --admin override path only if genuinely warranted and justified in the PR body, per GIT_MERGE.md). Use the commit/PR summary from DOC-UPDATER's result.summary (handoffs/WF02-REQ367-20260917/step-06-doc-updater.json) as the basis for the PR description. State plainly in the PR body that this requirement does NOT make the QA deploy live (companion ai-dala-infra credential task required separately).

Complete the handoff: status COMPLETED, result.status PASS/FAIL, git_evidence (branch, commits, PR URL, merge SHA, push_status), next_action. Commit the completed handoff on the feature branch before the final merge if possible, or in a small follow-up PR if the branch is already merged by the time this is written (matching GIT_MERGE.md's own documented pattern for finalizing Step Final's own record).

issues.description: CORRECTED (2026-09-17, after this handoff's initial write): this run's own ELIXIR-DEV Step Final dispatch (agent aef05cb56954742fd) had reported its local mix test run appeared stalled -- zero streamed output for an extended period despite the underlying erl.exe process staying alive -- and ORCH took over Step Final on that basis, relying on CI as the authoritative gate instead of waiting further. The local run was NOT actually stalled: it completed on its own after ~50 minutes (3018.1s) with a genuinely clean result -- `Finished in 3018.1 seconds (28.7s async, 2989.3s sync); Result: 4335 passed (6 properties, 4329 tests), 23 excluded; exited with code 0` -- reported back to ORCH after this run had already merged via CI. The earlier 'zero bytes of output' read that looked like a stall was itself a race against a buffered/not-yet-flushed output file, not a real hang. Downgraded from MAJOR to MINOR and corrected here rather than left standing as a false finding: this run's actual outcome (CI green, local suite also fully clean, 0 failures either way) was never in doubt, but the original stall diagnosis was wrong and should not be cited as evidence of a real local-suite hang class in any future docs/anti-patterns.md entry without re-verifying first.

Three of this run's own ORCH-authored handoff dispatches (step-02c, step-02d, step-06) had fabricated sequential-narrative timestamps instead of real clock reads, only caught by CI's own lint_handoffs gate rather than at dispatch time. Corrected in this run (see step-02c/02d/06's own orch_timestamp_correction notes); worth reinforcing at dispatch time in future runs -- ORCH should read the real clock at each dispatch, not narrate a plausible-sounding sequence.
